title: Otto's ModdedMC Server
welcome: Welcome to Otto's ModdedMC Server! You start in an ordinary Overworld with a torch, a coffee and a slice of toast. This guide covers the whole pack: the original SkyFactory 3 progression rebuilt for a normal world, plus Create, the Twilight Forest and the Aether.

The Recommended tab lists every goal in one proven order, split into six ages. Just do the next unticked goal: nothing in the list needs something from further down. By Type groups goals by activity and By Mod by mod.

Click any goal to open its hint panel: why it is worth doing, step-by-step instructions, what to bring, pictures of portals and multiblocks, and every recipe for the items involved. Hover an item for its name; click it to see how to make it in JEI (right-click: what it is used in). Click the panel's x or the goal again to close it.
At a crafting table? Press G (or the book button) to open this guide on top of it. The + beside a recipe puts the items into the grid for you, like JEI. Shift-click + for as many as you can make.
Tick a goal with its checkbox. Progress is shared by everyone on the server and saved with the world; hovering a ticked box shows who completed it.

goals.text: Gather wood and make a Crafting Table
goals.hint: Punch a tree for logs, turn them into planks, then put 4 planks in a 2x2 square.
goals.why: Almost every recipe in the pack needs a 3x3 crafting grid. A crafting table is the first thing everyone builds.
goals.tip: Open this guide while the crafting table is open (press G) and click + next to a recipe to fill the grid automatically.
steps: Hold left-click on a tree trunk to break logs. Collect 4 or more.
Open your inventory (E) and put a log in the 2x2 grid to get 4 planks.
Fill the 2x2 grid with planks to make a Crafting Table, then place it and right-click it.
Make sticks (2 planks stacked) for tools, and plant the saplings that fall from leaves.

goals.text: Make a stone pickaxe and a furnace
goals.hint: Mine cobblestone with a wooden pickaxe. 8 cobblestone in a ring makes a furnace.
goals.why: Stone tools last much longer than wood, and the furnace cooks food, smelts ores and makes charcoal for torches.
steps: Make a wooden pickaxe (3 planks over 2 sticks).
Dig down a few blocks anywhere to reach stone; mining it gives cobblestone.
Make a stone pickaxe, axe and sword with cobblestone.
Put 8 cobblestone in a ring for a furnace. Smelt logs into charcoal and make torches (charcoal over a stick).

goals.text: Recover your items from a Gravestone after dying
goals.hint: When you die, a gravestone keeps your items where you fell. Right-click or break it to get them back.
goals.why: A gravestone keeps the inventory dropped at death together so you can recover it. Plan a safe return route before approaching it.
goals.tip: A grave is a recovery aid, not a guarantee against every modded hazard. Avoid deliberately testing it with valuable gear.
steps: Read the death location on the obituary or JourneyMap death marker.
Return with spare food and tools, secure the area, then break your gravestone to recover its contents.
Check that you recovered your equipment before leaving.

goals.text: Open your map and save a waypoint at home
goals.hint: Press J for the JourneyMap map. Press B to create a waypoint where you stand.
goals.why: The world is huge and you will travel far for villages, structures and portals. A home waypoint always leads you back.
goals.tip: Use Controls to resolve conflicting keybindings; several mods may use B.
steps: Press J to open JourneyMap, or find its fullscreen-map binding in Controls.
Open Waypoints, create a waypoint at your base and name it Home.
Check its dimension and visibility settings.

goals.text: Claim your base chunks so they are protected
goals.hint: Open the FTB Chunks map (M) and drag across chunks to claim them for your team.
goals.why: Claimed chunks protect your builds from other players and from explosions, and you can force-load them later so machines keep running.
steps: Press M to open the FTB Chunks claim map.
Left-click and drag over the chunks around your base to claim them.
Invite friends to your team (FTB Teams) so they can build there too.

goals.text: Sleep through your first night in a bed
goals.hint: Three wool (from sheep) above three planks makes a bed. Sleeping also sets your respawn point.
goals.why: Night brings zombies, skeletons and creepers. A bed skips the night and makes you respawn at home instead of at world spawn.
steps: Collect three wool of the same color and three planks.
Craft a bed and place it in a lit, enclosed shelter with room above it.
Use the bed at night to sleep and set your respawn point.

mobs.where: Spawns naturally in Bamboo Jungle, Birch Forest, Cherry Grove, Dark Forest and 13 more (the Overworld). Lead them home with their favourite food and breed two of them to get more.

goals.text: Hang a Hammock to rest during the day
goals.hint: Hammocks hang between two fences or walls and let you skip the day without changing your spawn.
goals.why: A hammock skips the day, which helps when you want night-only things (mob hunting, certain crops) without losing your bed spawn.
steps: Craft a hammock and its matching support items shown in JEI.
Place the supports and hammock using the item placement preview, leaving the sleeping space clear.
Use the hammock during the day to rest until night. Keep a bed for your home respawn point.

goals.text: Make a bucket and carry water and lava
goals.hint: Three iron ingots in a V make a bucket. Water puts out fires and makes farmland; lava is great fuel.
goals.why: Buckets are needed for farms, Nether and Aether portals, cobblestone generators, Ex Nihilo barrels and to escape lava. A lava bucket smelts 100 items.
steps: Smelt 3 raw iron into ingots (caves, see the next goals, or a village chest).
Craft a bucket: iron ingots in a V shape.
Fill it at any water source. Make a second bucket and fill it from a lava pool (careful!).
Make an infinite water source: dig a 2x2 hole and pour water into two opposite corners.

goals.text: Go limp as a ragdoll and get back up
goals.hint: Press H to flop over as a physics ragdoll; press Shift to stand up again.
goals.why: Sable Ragdolls turns you into a floppy physics body: great for jokes, falls off airships and dramatic screenshots. You keep all your items.
goals.tip: Hard impacts while ragdolled hurt, just like falling. Do not ragdoll next to a cliff or lava.
steps: Press H (Options > Controls > Sable Ragdolls to change the key). You tumble and keep any momentum you had.
Hold W, A, S or D to roll around while limp.
Press Shift to get back up (after about 3 seconds).
Friends can grab and drag your ragdoll with the mouse buttons shown on screen.

goals.text: Explore a cave and return with coal, iron and copper
goals.hint: Caves and cliffs expose ores. Smelt raw iron and raw copper in a furnace.
goals.why: Iron is the most important early metal: tools, buckets, armor, hoppers and most machines need it. Coal keeps your furnaces and torches going.
goals.tip: Fortune pickaxes give extra raw ore. Mining iron at Y 16 to 64 works well; very deep caves also have diamonds.
steps: Bring torches, food, a stone pickaxe and spare blocks.
Explore exposed caves carefully and light the paths you use.
Mine coal, raw iron and raw copper, then return before supplies run low.
Smelt the raw metals in a furnace.

goals.text: Mine a whole ore vein at once with Vein Miner
goals.hint: Hold the Vein Miner key (default `) while breaking an ore to mine the connected vein.
goals.why: Vein mining saves a lot of time and pickaxe swings on every ore vein and tree.
steps: Find an ore vein (or a tree).
Hold the Vein Miner key (default ` , the key under Esc) and break one block.
All connected blocks of the same kind break too, using durability and hunger per block.

goals.text: Smelt iron and make a full set of iron tools
goals.hint: Iron pickaxe, axe, shovel and sword. You need iron to mine diamonds and gold.
goals.why: An iron pickaxe is required to mine diamonds, gold, redstone and many modded ores. Iron tools are fast and durable.
steps: Smelt about 10 raw iron into ingots.
Craft the pickaxe first (3 iron over 2 sticks), then the sword, axe and shovel.

goals.text: Wear a full set of iron armor and carry a shield
goals.hint: Helmet, chestplate, leggings and boots from 24 iron, plus a shield (planks and one iron).
goals.why: Armor cuts the damage you take by more than half, and a shield blocks arrows, creeper blasts and melee hits. You will need both for caves and the Nether.
steps: Smelt 24 iron ingots (and 1 more for the shield).
Craft helmet, chestplate, leggings and boots.
Craft a shield and hold it in your off-hand (F swaps hands). Right-click to block.

goals.text: Find a village and trade with a villager
goals.hint: Villages spawn in plains, deserts, savannas, taigas and snowy plains. Right-click a villager that has a job.
goals.why: Villages have free food, beds and loot chests, and villagers trade useful items (books, tools, food) for emeralds. Emeralds also buy seeds at the Market later.
goals.tip: Zombies can kill villagers or convert them, depending on difficulty. Light and enclose the village before night.
steps: Explore plains, deserts, savannas, taigas or snowy plains for a village.
Mark it in JourneyMap using J and Waypoints.
Right-click an adult villager with a profession to see its offers.
Trade a requested crop or material for emeralds; protect villagers and their workstations.

mobs.where: Villagers live in villages (plains, desert, savanna, taiga and snowy plains). Get more by giving them beds and food (bread, carrots) so they breed, or cure a zombie villager with a splash potion of weakness and a golden apple.

goals.text: Set up a crop plot and bring animals back to your base
goals.hint: Hoe dirt next to water and plant seeds from grass. Hold wheat to lead cows and sheep home.
goals.why: A farm means endless food, and breeding animals gives leather, wool and meat. Wheat, carrots and potatoes are also used by many mods.
steps: Break tall grass to collect wheat seeds.
Make a hoe and till dirt next to water (water hydrates 4 blocks in every direction).
Plant the seeds; they need light to grow.
Hold wheat: cows and sheep follow you. Fence them in and breed them (wheat on two adults).

mobs.where: Spawns naturally in Bamboo Jungle, Birch Forest, Dark Forest, Forest and 11 more (the Overworld). Lead them home with their favourite food and breed two of them to get more.

goals.text: Apply a block to a sheep with Shear Madness
goals.hint: Use a full block on a sheep to dress it in that block.
goals.why: Shear Madness lets adult sheep wear supported blocks; shearing returns the block.
goals.tip: The sheep does not need to be sheared first. Some coverings have special behavior; TNT-covered sheep explode when killed.
steps: Find an adult sheep and hold a block with a solid collision shape.
Right-click the sheep with the block to apply its appearance.
Use shears to remove the covering and recover the block.

mobs.where: Spawns naturally in Bamboo Jungle, Birch Forest, Cherry Grove, Dark Forest and 13 more (the Overworld). Lead them home with their favourite food and breed two of them to get more.

goals.text: Shear a block-covered sheep to restore its wool coat
goals.hint: Shears remove the block and give it back.
goals.why: You get your block back, and the sheep regrows normal wool for your beds and banners.
steps: Craft shears (two iron ingots placed diagonally).
Right-click the block-dressed sheep with the shears.
The block drops and the sheep has its wool coat again.

goals.text: Shear a sheep with Wooden Shears
goals.hint: Cheap early shears made from planks.
goals.why: Wooden shears get wool, leaves and vines before you have iron to spare.
steps: Craft wooden shears (recipe below).
Right-click a sheep to get 1-3 wool without killing it.

goals.text: Make a Cutting Board and a Pot from Pam's HarvestCraft
goals.hint: Pam's tools are reusable crafting ingredients for hundreds of foods; check JEI with U on the tool.
goals.why: Pam's foods restore much more hunger and saturation than plain crops. The tools are never used up.
steps: Craft the Cutting Board and the Pot (recipes below). Also useful: Skillet, Saucepan, Bakeware, Mixing Bowl, Juicer.
Put a tool in the crafting grid with ingredients. The tool stays in the grid.
Press U on a tool in JEI to see every food it makes.

goals.text: Cook a meal with Pam's HarvestCraft
goals.hint: Use your cooking tools with crops: apple pie, grilled cheese, noodle soup and many more.
goals.why: Big meals keep you full for a long time, so you spend less time eating and more time building.
steps: Gather ingredients from your farm, village gardens and Pam crops (wild gardens drop seeds).
Open JEI, search for a meal and press R to see what it needs.
Craft it with the right tool in the grid.

goals.text: Turn coal or charcoal into Mini Coal
goals.hint: One coal makes 8 mini coal; each smelts exactly one item, so small jobs waste nothing.
goals.why: A coal smelts 8 items. If you only need to smelt 2, mini coal saves the rest.
steps: Put one coal (or charcoal) in the crafting grid for 8 mini coal.
Use one mini coal per item you smelt.

goals.text: Climb with stepladders or Climbing Rope
goals.hint: Stepladders and climbing rope are easy ways up a wall.
goals.why: A quick and cheap way up cliffs and into mines without building stairs.
steps: Craft stepladders or climbing rope (recipes below).
Place stepladders against a wall and walk up; place rope from the top and it hangs down.

goals.text: Speed up sugar cane with Snad
goals.hint: Plant sugar cane on Snad beside water and compare its growth with an ordinary plot.
goals.why: Snad is a special growth-boosting block. Ordinary sand does not inherently grow sugar cane faster than dirt.
steps: Craft Snad using the recipe below.
Place it beside water and plant sugar cane on top.
Keep the farm loaded and leave vertical space for growth; harvest the upper cane to keep the plant growing.

goals.text: Twerk a Sapling into a Tree
goals.hint: Crouch repeatedly next to saplings and crops to make them grow (TS2K16).
goals.why: Twerking (crouching repeatedly) is free bonemeal. It speeds up saplings and crops when you are waiting for wood or food.
goals.tip: Growth attempts can take time. Give the sapling light and enough clear space; bone meal can help but does not guarantee a tree on every use.
steps: Stand next to a sapling or a crop.
Tap the crouch key (Shift) quickly and repeatedly.
Green particles show it is working.

goals.text: Use a Crook on leaves to get saplings and a Silkworm
goals.hint: Craft a crook from sticks and break leaves with it for extra saplings and the odd silkworm.
goals.why: The SkyFactory sifting tools turn common blocks into ores, seeds and more. They are a renewable backup when caves run dry. The crook drops more saplings and finds Silkworms for string.
steps: Craft a crook from sticks (recipe below).
Break leaves with it: more saplings drop, and about 1 in 100 leaves drops a silkworm.

goals.text: Compost leaves or saplings in a Wooden Barrel to make Dirt
goals.hint: Right-click a wooden barrel with leaves, saplings or food. When full it slowly becomes dirt.
goals.why: Dirt from compost is renewable, which matters for farms and for sieving dirt into seeds and pebbles.
steps: Craft a wooden barrel (recipe below).
Right-click it with leaves, saplings, seeds, food or rotten flesh until it is full.
Wait: the compost turns into a block of dirt. Right-click to take it out.

goals.text: Collect rain water in a Wooden Barrel
goals.hint: An empty wooden barrel left out in the rain slowly fills with water.
goals.why: An open barrel gathers water during Overworld rain, useful before you have a permanent water supply.
steps: Place an empty wooden barrel outdoors in a biome where rain reaches the ground.
Leave the sky above it clear and wait for rain.
Use a bucket once it contains enough water. In dry dimensions or biomes, fill it from a bucket instead.

goals.text: Infest leaves with a Silkworm and crook them for string
goals.hint: Use a silkworm on leaves, wait until they turn white with webs, then break them with a crook.
goals.why: String makes the String Mesh for the sieve, plus wool, bows and fishing rods, without hunting spiders.
steps: Right-click a leaf block with a silkworm.
Wait until the leaves turn completely white (the infestation spreads).
Break the white leaves with the crook for string (and sometimes more silkworms).

mobs.where: Spawns naturally in most biomes of the Overworld; The Beneath (the Beneath); Highlands Underground, Spooky Forest, Underground (the Twilight Forest), in the dark or at night. Mob spawners for it are found in the Deep Dark dimension, the Overworld, the Beneath (dungeons and other structures).

Spawns naturally in Sulfur Caves (the Overworld); The Beneath (the Beneath), in the dark or at night. Mob spawners for it are found in the Deep Dark dimension, the Overworld (dungeons and other structures).

goals.text: Craft a Sieve and a String Mesh
goals.hint: Put the mesh in the sieve, then right-click it with gravel, sand or dust to sift.
goals.why: A sieve turns gravel, sand, dust and dirt into ores, gems, seeds and pebbles. It is the heart of SkyFactory resource gathering.
steps: Craft the sieve and a string mesh (9 string).
Right-click the sieve with the mesh to insert it.
Right-click the sieve with gravel (or sand, dust, dirt), then keep right-clicking until it is sifted.
Place several sieves next to each other: one click sifts all of them.

goals.text: Craft a Hammer to turn Cobblestone into Gravel, Sand and Dust
goals.hint: Hammers turn cobblestone into gravel, gravel into sand and sand into dust.
goals.why: Gravel, sand and dust are what you put in the sieve. A hammer turns endless cobblestone into all three.
steps: Craft a hammer (recipe below).
Place cobblestone and break it with the hammer: it drops gravel.
Place and hammer gravel for sand, then sand for dust.

goals.text: Sift Gravel, Sand and Dust in a Sieve for ore pieces
goals.hint: Sifting gravel gives ore chunks; four chunks craft an ore block you can smelt.
goals.why: A renewable source of iron, copper, gold, zinc and other ores, plus diamonds, emeralds and lapis from gravel.
goals.tip: JEI shows every sieve drop and its chance: press U on gravel, sand or dust.
steps: Sift gravel with a String Mesh (or better).
Ore chunks drop by chance: iron, copper, gold, zinc, lead, silver, nickel, aluminum.
Craft 4 chunks of one metal into an ore block (recipe below) and smelt it.
Sift sand for nuggets and prismarine, dust for redstone, glowstone, gunpowder and blaze powder, and dirt for seeds.

goals.text: Upgrade your Sieve mesh and enchant it
goals.hint: Iron and diamond meshes give rarer drops; Fortune and Efficiency enchantments work on meshes.
goals.why: Better meshes give more and rarer drops (more diamonds, golden items); Fortune adds rolls and Efficiency sifts faster.
steps: Craft a flint mesh, then an iron, golden or diamond mesh (recipes below).
Enchant the mesh at an enchanting table or with books on an anvil.
Swap meshes depending on what you want: JEI lists drops per mesh.

goals.text: Make Clay by putting Dust into a water-filled Barrel
goals.hint: Fill a barrel with water first, then right-click it with dust.
goals.why: Clay makes bricks, Tinkers grout, porcelain and the crucible. This makes it without finding a river.
steps: Fill a wooden barrel with water (bucket or rain).
Right-click it with dust from the hammer.
A clay block appears; right-click to take it.

goals.text: Store bulk items in Storage Drawers
goals.hint: Each drawer holds many of one item; a Drawer Controller links them into one inventory.
goals.why: Chests fill up fast with cobblestone, dirt and ores. A drawer holds 32 stacks of one item and shows what is inside.
steps: Craft a drawer and place it with its front accessible.
Right-click its front while holding the item to deposit it; double-right-click deposits matching inventory items.
Left-click the front to withdraw one item; sneak-left-click to withdraw a stack.
Add a storage upgrade when the drawer fills, and label or lock drawers as needed.

goals.text: Build a Sophisticated Storage barrel or chest
goals.hint: Craft a storage chest or barrel, then use its inventory and storage-specific upgrades.
goals.why: These chests can be upgraded in place (iron, gold, diamond, netherite) and accept upgrades that pick up, compact, smelt or void items.
steps: Craft the storage block shown below and place it.
Open it to store items, then use its upgrade slots for compatible storage upgrades.
Check each upgrade tooltip and JEI recipe before buying materials; backpack upgrades are a separate set.

goals.text: Craft a Charset Barrel and store items in it
goals.hint: A Charset barrel holds up to 4096 of one item and works with automation.
goals.why: A cheap bulk barrel for one item type, great for cobblestone, seeds or wood.
steps: Craft the barrel (recipe below).
Right-click with an item to store it; left-click to take a stack.
Hoppers and pipes can insert and extract.

goals.text: Carry a Sophisticated Backpack
goals.hint: Backpacks hold extra items and accept upgrades.
goals.why: Extra inventory space on long trips. Backpacks keep their contents when broken or dropped.
goals.tip: Try pickup and feeding upgrades as you expand. Test their filters with expendable items before relying on them.
steps: Craft a backpack and right-click it while held to open it.
Store supplies and add compatible upgrades in its upgrade slots.
Use the configured Open Backpack key when carrying or wearing it; resolve conflicts in Controls.

goals.text: Harvest a wide area with a Scythe
goals.hint: Scythes cut crops and grass in a large area.
goals.why: Harvesting big fields one block at a time is slow. A scythe cuts a large area of crops and grass per swing.
steps: Craft an iron scythe (recipe below).
Swing it at grown crops or tall grass: everything around breaks at once.

goals.text: Make a Watering Can
goals.hint: Hold right-click on crops to grow them faster. The reinforced can covers more.
goals.why: Watering cans speed up crops and saplings around you while you hold right-click.
steps: Craft a watering can (recipe below) and fill it at water.
Hold right-click while looking at crops or saplings.

goals.text: Trade at the Market for seeds and saplings
goals.hint: The Market sells seeds, saplings and Natura trees for emeralds.
goals.why: The Market sells seeds and saplings you cannot easily find, including Natura trees, Pam's crops and flowers.
steps: Craft the Market (recipe below) and place it.
Right-click it, browse the categories and pay with emeralds.

goals.text: Buy a Natura sapling from the Market
goals.hint: Natura's Overworld trees do not generate here; buy their saplings at the Market.
goals.why: Natura woods (maple, silverbell, amaranth, tiger) give unique planks and decorations.
steps: Open the Market and find the Natura saplings.
Buy one with emeralds and plant it like a normal sapling.

goals.text: Sift Topiary Grass to collect Natura saplings
goals.hint: Sift Topiary Grass for Natura Overworld saplings; Nether species use the soul-sand route.
goals.why: Sifting supplies saplings when the pack disables their natural tree generation.
steps: Make Topiary Grass with the recipe shown below.
Sift it using a mesh accepted by its JEI sieving recipe.
Plant and farm the saplings. Check soul-sand sieving for Nether species.

goals.text: Break grass to find Natura barley and cotton seeds
goals.hint: Natura seeds drop from grass at a low chance.
goals.why: Barley makes flour and bread; cotton makes string and wool, another string source.
steps: Break tall grass: barley and cotton seeds drop at a low chance.
Plant them on farmland like wheat.

goals.text: Build with Missing Pieces chairs, tables and wedges
goals.hint: Extra shapes for many blocks. Wood copies of vanilla shapes come from the stonecutter.
goals.why: Chairs, tables, wedges and corners give builds detail that plain blocks cannot. You can sit on the chairs.
steps: Wood shapes come from the stonecutter (put planks in); others are crafted (recipes below).
Place them like blocks: wedges and corners turn to face you.
Right-click a chair to sit on it.

goals.text: Craft Graphite from Charcoal
goals.hint: Two charcoal in a crafting grid make two graphite.
goals.why: Graphite is a cheap black dye made from charcoal, so you do not need to hunt squids for ink.
steps: Smelt logs in a furnace to make charcoal.
Put 2 charcoal in the crafting grid: you get 2 graphite.

goals.text: Use Graphite to dye White Wool Black
goals.hint: Graphite works as a black dye.
goals.why: Black wool for builds and beds, using only charcoal.
steps: Put white wool and graphite in the crafting grid (recipe below).
Graphite works in most recipes that take black dye.

goals.text: Move a full chest with Packing Tape
goals.hint: Tape up a chest or machine to pick it up with everything inside.
goals.why: Moving a full chest normally means emptying it. Tape lets you pick it up with everything inside.
steps: Craft Packing Tape and use it on a supported chest or storage block.
Break the wrapped block to collect its packed item.
Place the package at the destination and unpack it. Test an empty container first if you are unsure whether a modded block is supported.

goals.text: Pick up a chest with Carry On
goals.hint: Sneak and right-click a block or animal with empty hands to carry it.
goals.why: Carry On moves supported containers without unloading them.
goals.tip: You walk slower while carrying. You cannot carry blocks that other players own in claimed chunks.
steps: Empty both hands, approach a supported chest and hold the configured Carry On key while right-clicking it.
Walk to the destination and right-click to place it.
Check the inventory after placing it. Support and claim permissions can restrict what you can carry.

goals.text: Mine diamonds and make a diamond pickaxe
goals.hint: Diamonds are most common deep down near Y -58. You need an iron pickaxe to mine them.
goals.why: A diamond pickaxe mines obsidian (for the Nether portal) and diamonds are needed for enchanting, the Twilight Forest portal and many machines.
goals.tip: Sifting gravel with a better mesh also gives diamonds over time.
steps: Bring an iron pickaxe, torches, food and a water bucket (to turn lava into obsidian).
Dig down to around Y -58 (press F3 to see your height) and branch-mine: 1x2 tunnels 3 blocks apart.
Diamonds also show up in caves near lava; mine them with an iron (or better) pickaxe.
Craft a diamond pickaxe from 3 diamonds and 2 sticks.

goals.text: Build an Enchanting Table and enchant a tool
goals.hint: Diamonds, obsidian and a book make the table; 15 bookshelves around it unlock level 30 enchantments.
goals.why: Efficiency, Fortune, Unbreaking and Protection make everything faster and safer. Fortune multiplies ores; Looting multiplies mob drops.
steps: Collect obsidian: pour water over still lava and mine it with a diamond pickaxe.
Craft the enchanting table (2 diamonds, 4 obsidian, 1 book).
Craft up to 15 bookshelves (planks + 3 books each) and place them 1 block away from the table, at the same height or one higher.
Put a tool and lapis lazuli in the table and pick an enchantment.

diagram.title: Bookshelf layout
diagram.view: Top view: 15 bookshelves with a 1-block gap around the table
diagram.note: Leave the gap free (no torches or carpet). Stack a second layer of shelves if you run out of floor space.

goals.text: Repair and combine enchantments on an Anvil
goals.hint: An anvil joins two tools or a tool and an enchanted book, and renames items.
goals.why: Anvils fix enchanted tools without losing their enchantments and let you add enchanted books from villagers or loot.
steps: Craft an anvil (3 iron blocks over 4 iron ingots).
Put a damaged tool and a matching material (or a second tool) in the anvil.
Put a tool and an enchanted book in to add the book enchantment.

goals.text: Make Grout and fire it into Seared Bricks
goals.hint: Grout is sand, gravel and clay; smelt it into seared bricks.
goals.why: Seared bricks are the building material for Tinkers melting equipment and smelteries.
steps: Craft grout from sand, gravel and clay using JEI.
Smelt grout into seared bricks.
Use the smeltery diagram and block list to budget the controller, tank, drain, casting equipment and walls before building.

goals.text: Craft a Part Builder and a Tinker Station
goals.hint: Tinkers tools are built from parts and can be repaired and upgraded instead of replaced.
goals.why: The Part Builder makes nonmetal tool parts; the Tinker Station assembles, repairs and modifies compatible tools.
goals.tip: This pack uses Tinkers 3 modifiers and slots. It does not include the old TinkerToolLeveling XP system.
steps: Craft a Pattern (planks and sticks) and a Part Builder.
Craft a Tinker Station.
Place a Pattern Chest nearby if you like; the station shows all tool layouts on the left.

goals.text: Make a Tinkers' tool from a head, handle and binding
goals.hint: Make parts in the Part Builder from patterns, then assemble them in the Tinker Station.
goals.why: Even a flint or copper Tinkers pickaxe can be repaired and leveled, and its parts can be swapped later.
goals.tip: Use the Tinkers books and tool tooltip for material traits and modifier slots. Using a tool does not award leveling XP in this pack.
steps: Use patterns in the Part Builder to make the required parts from craftable materials such as wood, flint or bone.
Open the Tinker Station, select the tool and place its required parts in the outlined slots.
Take the assembled tool and inspect its material traits. Metal parts are made by casting later.

goals.text: Build a Tinkers' Construct smeltery for processing ore
goals.hint: Seared bricks make the walls, controller, drain, tank and faucet. Melting ore gives extra metal.
goals.why: Melting raw ore gives more metal than smelting, and the smeltery casts tool parts and alloys bronze, rose gold and more.
goals.tip: The Tinkers books (Materials and You, Puny Smelting, Mighty Smelting) explain every material and structure.
steps: Build a floor of Seared Bricks, then walls one block high around the inside space.
Put the Smeltery Controller in a wall (facing out), plus a Seared Drain and a Seared Fuel Tank in the walls.
Fill the tank with lava (bucket). The controller lights up when the structure is valid.
Put a Faucet on the outside of the drain and a Casting Table or Casting Basin under it.
Put ores into the controller; right-click the faucet to pour molten metal into ingot casts.

diagram.title: Smallest smeltery
diagram.view: A 3x3 floor with a ring of walls on top; the middle stays empty.
diagram.note: Bigger smelteries (more walls, taller) melt more at once. The Faucet goes on the outside of the Drain.

goals.text: Cast a metal tool part and upgrade an existing tool with it
goals.hint: Pour molten metal from a smeltery faucet onto a casting table holding a cast.
goals.why: Metal parts (iron, cobalt, manyullyn) give much better stats. Casts are reusable moulds.
steps: Place a disposable craftable tool part, such as a wooden pick head, on a Casting Table.
Pour the cast-making metal specified by JEI over it; making a gold cast consumes the sample part.
Melt the desired metal and pour it into the completed reusable cast.
Use the metal part with your tool in the appropriate Tinkers station to replace that part.

goals.text: Make a Mattock
goals.hint: A shovel-and-axe hybrid, great for clearing land.
goals.why: One tool digs dirt and chops wood at full speed, so clearing land for a base is much faster.
steps: In the Tinker Station pick the mattock layout to see the parts it needs.
Make the parts in the Part Builder (or cast metal ones).
Assemble them in the Tinker Station.

goals.text: Add a modifier to a Tinkers' tool
goals.hint: Use the Tinkers books and available modifier slots to improve a tool.
goals.why: Modifiers add useful abilities such as mining speed or damage. The old XP-based tool-leveling add-on is not installed.
goals.tip: Tick this goal after applying a modifier. Existing completion marks are preserved.
steps: Inspect the tool tooltip for available upgrade and ability slots.
Find a compatible modifier recipe in the Tinkers books or JEI, such as Haste for a mining tool.
Apply its ingredients with the tool in the required station, then verify the modifier in the tooltip.

goals.text: Build a Tinkers' Sledge Hammer for mining three-by-three
goals.hint: Broad tools mine a 3x3 area.
goals.why: Mines a 3x3 area per swing: perfect for digging rooms, tunnels and quarries.
steps: Cast large parts: a hammer head, tough handle and two large plates (casts or the Part Builder).
Assemble the sledge hammer in a Tinkers Anvil (forge layout).

goals.text: Build an underground workshop connected to your home
goals.hint: A safe workshop keeps machines and storage away from mobs.
goals.why: The next ages add many machines. A lit, enclosed workshop keeps mobs and creepers away from them.
goals.tip: Light the workshop and seal entrances. Lighting prevents ordinary darkness-based spawning; special spawners and some modded mobs follow other rules.
steps: Excavate a room under or beside your home with space for machines and cables.
Light the floor, secure entrances and keep hazardous machinery separated.
Connect it to your home with stairs or an elevator.

goals.text: Travel between floors with Elevators
goals.hint: Stand on an elevator and jump to go up, sneak to go down.
goals.why: Instant travel between floors of a tall base or down a deep mine shaft, without ladders or water.
steps: Craft two elevators (recipe below; dye them any color).
Place them in the same column, one per floor, with at least 2 blocks of air above each.
Stand on one: jump to go up to the next elevator, sneak to go down.

goals.text: Obtain Andesite Alloy for your first Create components
goals.hint: Mix andesite with iron nuggets (or zinc) in a crafting grid.
goals.why: Create is the pack's mechanical tech. Andesite alloy makes shafts, cogwheels, casings, belts and most early machines.
goals.tip: Hold W while hovering any Create item to watch a Ponder scene that shows how it works.
steps: Mine andesite (grey stone, common in caves and mountains).
Craft andesite with iron nuggets (or zinc nuggets) for andesite alloy.

goals.text: Make Shafts and Cogwheels to carry rotation
goals.hint: Hold W over a Create item to Ponder it and see how it works.
goals.why: Create machines run on rotation. Shafts and cogwheels move rotation from a source to your machines.
steps: Craft shafts (andesite alloy) and cogwheels (shaft + planks).
Shafts connect end to end; cogwheels connect side by side and change direction.

goals.text: Build a Create water-wheel workshop and connect a machine to it
goals.hint: Water flowing over a water wheel produces rotation.
goals.why: A water wheel is free, endless rotation to run your first Create machines.
steps: Craft a water wheel (recipe below).
Place it on a shaft and let flowing water run over it from the side or top.
Connect shafts and cogwheels from the wheel to a machine. Several wheels add their stress capacity together.

goals.text: Use a Mechanical Press to make a metal sheet
goals.hint: Put an ingot on a depot under a turning press.
goals.why: Iron, copper and gold sheets are needed by many Create recipes. The press also compacts items when placed over a basin.
steps: Craft the press and a depot.
Put the press 2 blocks above the depot and give it rotation.
Drop an ingot on the depot: it is pressed into a sheet.

goals.text: Connect two Shafts with a Mechanical Belt
goals.hint: Use a belt connector on two shafts; belts carry items and rotation.
goals.why: Belts move items between machines and are the backbone of every Create production line.
steps: Craft a belt connector (dried kelp).
Right-click one shaft, then another shaft in line (up to 20 blocks apart).

goals.text: Wash gravel or crushed ore with an Encased Fan and water
goals.hint: A fan blowing through water washes items: gravel gives iron nuggets and flint.
goals.why: Washing turns crushed ores into extra nuggets and gravel into flint and iron nuggets, a cheap renewable iron source.
steps: Craft an encased fan and give it rotation.
Place water in front of it (flowing water works).
Drop gravel or crushed ore into the air stream past the water.

goals.text: Combine ingredients with a Mechanical Mixer
goals.hint: A mixer above a basin combines items and fluids.
goals.why: Mixing makes alloys, dough, chocolate and later brass. Many recipes need it.
steps: Place a basin, the mixer 2 blocks above it, and give the mixer rotation.
Put ingredients into the basin; take outputs from it (or with a funnel).

goals.text: Automate a useful material with Create machinery
goals.hint: Pick a material you keep running out of and build a line for it.
goals.why: Automating one material teaches you belts, funnels and machines, and saves hours later.
steps: Pick a target: iron sheets, cobblestone (a mechanical drill on a cobble generator), gravel, bread ...
Feed inputs with funnels or a mechanical arm and send outputs to a chest.

goals.text: Assemble a Simulated Contraption with a Physics Assembler
goals.hint: Glue a group of blocks, put a Physics Assembler on them and pull its lever: they become a moving physics object.
goals.why: Create Aeronautics builds real moving vehicles. The Physics Assembler turns blocks into a contraption with weight and momentum that you can stand on, and chests and machines on it keep working.
goals.tip: Every block has a mass. Turn on advanced tooltips with F3+H and each block shows its Sable Mass: wood is light, iron and stone are heavy. A slime ball merges two contraptions.
steps: Craft a Physics Assembler: a lever above andesite casing, with andesite alloy on both sides (recipe below).
Build a small platform and place the assembler on top of it. It grabs the block under it.
Use Super Glue (or Honey Glue) on two corners to select every block that belongs to the contraption.
Hold right-click on the assembler and pull the lever. The blocks lift off the world and get physics.
To turn it back into normal blocks, use any Physics Assembler on the contraption again.

diagram.title: A first contraption
diagram.view: Layers from the bottom: a plank platform with the assembler on top
diagram.note: Glue the whole platform before you pull the lever. Pieces that are not connected split off as their own contraption.

goals.text: Lift off in a hot air balloon
goals.hint: A Hot Air Burner under a closed balloon of envelope blocks lifts a contraption into the air.
goals.why: Your first flying machine. A balloon carries you, your friends and cargo over mountains and oceans.
goals.tip: Hold W over the burner or an envelope to Ponder how balloons work. Right-click envelopes with dye to colour them. Torches and glowstone on board light up the ground below while you fly.
steps: Craft a Hot Air Burner (iron sheets, a block of coal, redstone and andesite alloy) and about 54 Hot Air Envelopes (wool and sticks).
Build a deck, put the burner in the middle and a Physics Assembler on the deck.
Build a closed box of envelopes above the burner, held up by fence posts. Hot air fills it from the top down, so the sides and top must be airtight; the bottom can stay open.
Glue the deck, posts and balloon, then pull the assembler lever.
Power the burner with redstone (a lever on it). It fills the balloon and the contraption rises. Turn the signal down or off to sink.

diagram.title: Small hot air balloon
diagram.view: Layers from the bottom: deck, burner, posts and a 5x5 balloon
diagram.note: A bigger balloon lifts more. Lift gets weaker the higher you fly, so the balloon settles where lift equals weight.

goals.text: Drive a car on Offroad wheels
goals.hint: Wheel Mounts with Tires turn a contraption into a ground vehicle.
goals.why: Cars carry you and cargo across land much faster than walking, and later Rock Cutting Wheels on a Borehead Bearing turn them into tunnel-boring machines.
goals.tip: Hold W over a Wheel Mount to Ponder it. Heavy cars need more rotation; check stress with Engineer's Goggles.
steps: Craft Springs (iron sheets and an iron nugget), then four Wheel Mounts (andesite casing, a spring, an iron sheet).
Craft four Tires (dried kelp around a shaft) and right-click each one onto a mount.
Build a chassis with the four mounts, a seat and a rotation source such as a Portable Engine, then glue it and assemble it with a Physics Assembler.
Rotation into the mounts drives the wheels. A redstone signal into a mount from the side steers it; from the top it brakes.

goals.text: Place Redstone Paste on a wall or ceiling
goals.hint: Redstone Paste sticks to walls and ceilings where dust cannot.
goals.why: Redstone paste runs signals up walls and across ceilings, which plain dust cannot do. Circuits stay small and hidden.
steps: Craft redstone paste (recipe below).
Right-click the side of a block or a ceiling: the paste sticks there.
It connects like redstone dust to neighbours on the same face.

goals.text: Power a redstone device through a Redstone Paste connection
goals.hint: Run paste up a wall to a lamp or door.
goals.why: Proves your wall wiring works: a lever at the floor controls a lamp near the ceiling.
steps: Place a lever at the bottom of a wall.
Run paste from the lever up the wall to a redstone lamp.
Flip the lever: the lamp lights up.

goals.text: Craft a Charset redstone gate
goals.hint: Gates face their output and read the sides. Try NAND, NOR, XOR or the RS latch.
goals.why: Logic gates replace big redstone torch contraptions with one small block.
steps: Craft a gate (recipes below).
Place it: the front is the output; the two sides (and back) are inputs.

goals.text: Use a Charset NAND Gate in a powered redstone circuit
goals.hint: Feed the sides with redstone and watch the output.
goals.why: Shows how gate logic works: a NAND gate is ON unless both inputs are ON. Every other gate can be built from NANDs.
steps: Place the gate; the front is the output.
Wire a lever to each side input and a lamp to the front.
Turn both levers on: the lamp turns off. Any other combination keeps it on.

goals.text: Rotate a Charset Gate with the Charset Wrench
goals.hint: The wrench rotates blocks that have a facing.
goals.why: Fix a gate (or most machines) that was placed facing the wrong way without breaking it and losing its settings.
steps: Craft the Charset wrench (recipe below).
Right-click the gate or machine to turn it.

goals.text: Chisel blocks into new designs
goals.hint: Put blocks into the chisel and pick a design.
goals.why: Hundreds of decorative variants of stone, wood, glass and more for nicer builds.
steps: Craft the chisel (recipe below).
Right-click to open it, put blocks in the input and click a design to convert the whole stack.

goals.text: Carve a block with Chisels & Bits
goals.hint: Left-click a block with a chisel to remove tiny bits; place bits with right-click.
goals.why: Build details at 1/16 block size: furniture, window frames, trims and statues.
steps: Place a chiselable block and hold a Chisels & Bits tool.
Select its edit mode using the tool controls shown in its tooltip or Controls menu.
Remove a small region, collect the bits, then place bits to build your design.
Use a Bit Bag or Bit Drawer to keep the materials organized.

goals.text: Make furniture at the Decobench
goals.hint: The Decomposer turns blocks into clay; the Decobench crafts decorations from it.
goals.why: Decocraft adds thousands of furniture and decoration models for homes, shops and towns.
steps: Craft a Decomposer and a Decobench (recipes below).
Put blocks into the Decomposer to turn them into decoration clay.
Use the clay at the Decobench to pick and craft furniture.

goals.text: Hang Fairy Lights between two fences
goals.hint: Right-click a fence with the lights, then another fence.
goals.why: Pretty string lights for paths, trees, markets and parties.
steps: Craft fairy lights (recipe below).
Right-click a fence post, walk to another fence and right-click it.
Right-click the string with dyes or lights to change it.

goals.text: Mix colors with Flat Colored Blocks
goals.hint: Use the paint mixer to make solid colored blocks.
goals.why: Exact solid colors for pixel art, signs and modern builds.
steps: Craft the paint mixer.
Combine dyes and blocks (JEI shows every color recipe).

goals.text: Build ramps and floors with the Platformer
goals.hint: The platformer makes ramps, floors and railings from planks.
goals.why: Quick wooden ramps, floors and railings for bridges, docks and stairs.
steps: Craft the platformer.
Put planks in, pick a shape (ramp, floor, railing) and take the result.

goals.text: Decorate with Reliquia lanterns, candles and sword plinths
goals.hint: Colored iron and gold lanterns, candle holders and sword plinths. Recipes in JEI.
goals.why: Decorative lighting in many colors, and a plinth to show off your best sword.
steps: Craft lanterns, candle holders or plinths (recipes below).
Right-click a sword plinth with a sword to display it.

goals.text: Fire Porcelain and build with Porcelain Bricks
goals.hint: Fire unfired porcelain in a furnace; dye it or make bricks from it.
goals.why: Clean white (or dyed) bricks for builds; porcelain also makes buckets and faucets.
steps: Craft unfired porcelain (clay and bone meal).
Smelt it into porcelain.
Craft porcelain bricks (and dye them if you like).

goals.text: Decorate with particle effect blocks
goals.hint: Particle blocks emit particles for decoration.
goals.why: Fire, smoke, hearts, notes or sparkles for fountains, fireplaces, shops and parties.
steps: Craft a particle block.
Right-click it to cycle through the effects.

goals.text: Write a checklist on a Clipboard
goals.hint: A clipboard holds a to-do list you can tick off.
goals.why: Keep your plans and shopping lists in-game, next to this guide.
steps: Craft a clipboard.
Right-click to open it and type a list.
Click a line to tick it off.

goals.text: Break glass without Silk Touch and collect Charset Glass Shards
goals.hint: Glass broken by hand drops shards.
goals.why: Broken glass is not wasted any more: the shards craft back into glass.
steps: Break a glass block with your hand or a normal tool.
Pick up the shards that drop.

obtain.sf3extras:charset_glass_shard: Break a glass block without Silk Touch.

goals.text: Craft a Glass Block from three Glass Shards
goals.hint: Three shards in a row make a glass block again.
goals.why: Turns broken glass back into blocks, so you never lose glass when rebuilding windows.
steps: Put three glass shards in a row in the crafting grid.

obtain.sf3extras:charset_glass_shard: Break a glass block without Silk Touch.

goals.text: Place a Charset Poster on a wall
goals.hint: Posters hang flat on a solid wall and show an item or map.
goals.why: Hang maps, items and art flat on a wall, like a picture frame without the frame.
steps: Craft a poster.
Place it on a solid wall and right-click it with an item or a map.

goals.text: Dye a minecart with a dye or Graphite
goals.hint: Right-click a minecart with a dye; the dye is not used up.
goals.why: Color-code minecarts on your rail lines so you know which cart goes where.
steps: Place a minecart on a rail.
Right-click it with a dye or graphite; the dye is not used up.

goals.text: Knock back primed TNT without resetting its fuse
goals.hint: Hit lit TNT to push it away; the fuse keeps counting.
goals.why: A Charset tweak that can save your base: hit a lit TNT block away from your walls.
steps: Far from your base, light a TNT block.
Hit the primed TNT: it flies away and the fuse keeps counting.

goals.text: Trigger the Zorro boost while falling toward a saddled horse
goals.hint: Fall more than two blocks onto a saddled horse and right-click it.
goals.why: A Charset stunt: land on your horse in style and it gets a speed boost.
steps: Tame and saddle a horse (saddles come from chests or fishing).
Jump from more than two blocks above it and right-click it while falling.

goals.text: Store items in a Simple Barrel
goals.hint: A wooden barrel that holds lots of one item.
goals.why: Another cheap bulk storage block for one item type, handy for seeds, cobblestone or dirt.
steps: Craft a simple barrel (recipe below).
Right-click with an item to store it; left-click to take a stack out.

goals.text: Upgrade a drawer with a Storage Upgrade
goals.hint: Storage upgrades multiply a drawer's capacity.
goals.why: One drawer can hold thousands of items with upgrades, so a small wall stores a whole mine.
steps: Craft a storage upgrade (obsidian is the first, then iron, gold, diamond, emerald).
Open the drawer (sneak-right-click with an empty hand) and put the upgrade in an upgrade slot.

goals.text: Pair a Charset Key with a Charset Barrel
goals.hint: Right-click an unlocked barrel with a key to pair them.
goals.why: Keys and locks keep your storage private on a shared server.
steps: Craft a key (recipe below).
Right-click an unlocked Charset barrel with it to pair them.

goals.text: Lock a Charset Barrel and unlock it with the matching key
goals.hint: Use the paired key to lock and unlock the barrel; a Master Key can bypass its lock.
goals.why: A barrel lock controls ordinary access, while claimed chunks provide separate protection for your base.
goals.tip: The Charset Master Key can unlock any Charset barrel. Do not treat this lock as owner-only multiplayer security.
steps: Pair a key with the barrel using the preceding goal.
Use the matching key to lock it, then verify ordinary interaction is blocked.
Use that key again to unlock it. Keep a recovery key somewhere safe.

goals.text: Craft a Charset Master Key
goals.hint: The Master Key unlocks any locked Charset barrel.
goals.why: A recovery tool for a lost paired key; it bypasses locks rather than checking ownership.
goals.tip: Use claims and server permissions for base protection. Keep this bypass tool secure.
steps: Craft the Master Key with the recipe below.
Use it on a locked Charset barrel to unlock it.

goals.text: Craft and place a Charset Shelf
goals.hint: A shelf shows and stores six item stacks.
goals.why: A display shelf: books, potions and trophies are visible and stored at the same time.
steps: Craft a shelf (recipe below) and place it on a wall or floor.
Right-click a slot on the shelf to put the item in your hand there.

goals.text: Craft, wear and open a Charset Backpack
goals.hint: Right-click to wear it, then press B to open its 27 slots.
goals.why: 27 extra slots that you wear on your back.
steps: Craft the backpack (recipe below).
Right-click to wear it.
Press B to open it.

goals.text: Create a 16x16x16 Colossal Chest
goals.hint: Fill the outline of a cube with chest walls and add a core. Bigger cubes hold more.
goals.why: One giant chest for everything: a 16x16x16 wooden one holds thousands of stacks.
goals.tip: This is a large storage challenge. Build a smaller valid chest first to learn the structure.
steps: Gather one Colossal Chest Core and enough compatible wall blocks for a hollow 16 x 16 x 16 outer shell.
Build all six faces, including floor and roof; leave the interior empty.
Replace one wall block with the Core and add an Interface where automation will connect.
Use the Core to confirm that the multiblock forms before filling it.

goals.text: Upgrade a chest to an Obsidian Chest
goals.hint: Use chest upgrades in order: wood -> iron -> gold -> diamond -> obsidian.
goals.why: Bigger chests (an obsidian chest holds 108 stacks and resists explosions). Four Obsidian Chests are part of the Quantum DSU recipe.
steps: Craft chest upgrades (wood to iron, iron to gold, gold to diamond, diamond to obsidian).
Right-click a placed chest with the upgrade; its contents stay inside.

goals.text: Craft and fire a Crucible, then melt Cobblestone into Lava
goals.hint: Fire the unfired porcelain crucible in a furnace, place it over a torch or lava, and feed it cobblestone.
goals.why: Endless lava from cobblestone: fuel for furnaces and generators, and obsidian when mixed with water.
steps: Craft porcelain clay (clay + bone meal), then an unfired crucible, and smelt it.
Place the crucible on top of a heat source: torch (slow), lava or fire (faster).
Right-click it with cobblestone; it melts into lava. Take it with a bucket.

goals.text: Make Obsidian in a Stone Barrel
goals.hint: Fill a stone barrel with lava, then right-click it with a water bucket.
goals.why: Renewable obsidian for portals, enchanting tables and obsidian chests.
steps: Craft a stone barrel.
Fill it with lava (bucket).
Right-click with a water bucket: it becomes obsidian.

goals.text: Craft the Tiny Progressions Cobblestone Generator
goals.hint: It makes cobblestone by itself. Pull it out with a hopper or pipe.
goals.why: Endless cobblestone with no water or lava: feed it to hammers (gravel, sand, dust), crucibles (lava) and compressors.
steps: Craft the cobblestone generator (recipe below).
Put a hopper or pipe under it leading into a chest or a drawer.
Higher tiers make cobblestone faster.

goals.text: Automate your Cobblestone with an Iron Cobblestone Generator
goals.hint: Higher tiers (iron, diamond, blaze, emerald) make cobblestone faster.
goals.why: More cobblestone per second for bigger sieving and crushing setups.
steps: Craft the iron tier from the basic generator and iron (recipe below).
Swap it in; later tiers are diamond, blaze and emerald.

goals.text: Make Fertilized Farmland
goals.hint: Rich or healthy fertilized farmland grows faster or gives extra crops.
goals.why: Rich farmland grows crops faster; healthy farmland gives an extra crop now and then.
steps: Craft a fertilizer (recipe below).
Right-click farmland with it.

obtain.farmingforblockheads:fertilized_farmland: Not crafted: use Rich Fertilizer on farmland.

goals.text: Grow corn and make popcorn
goals.hint: Plant kernels (from grass), harvest corn cobs and cook them into roasted corn, popcorn or chowder.
goals.why: Corn is another crop for food and recipes; popcorn and roasted corn are fun snacks.
steps: Break tall grass for corn kernels.
Plant them on farmland; corn grows two blocks tall.
Harvest the cobs and cook them into popcorn or roasted corn.

obtain.sf3extras:corn_cob: Harvest grown corn. Plant kernels, which drop from tall grass.

goals.text: Make a grass field away from your base for spawning animals
goals.hint: Animals spawn on grass in light; fence a large field.
goals.why: A lit grass area in a suitable biome can support passive animals and gives you room to breed them.
steps: Prepare a grassy enclosure with light and space above it in an animal-spawning biome.
Wait at a suitable distance while the area remains loaded; natural spawning also depends on mob caps.
If animals do not appear, lead or transport existing animals home and breed them.

goals.text: Prepare a farming space for several crops
goals.hint: Hydrated farmland, light and fences keep a farm growing day and night.
goals.why: Many mods need different crops; a big farm keeps them all stocked.
steps: Till soil around water channels (every 9x9 with water in the middle).
Light the farm so crops grow at night.
Fence it to keep animals out.

goals.text: Keep farmland wet with HydroGel
goals.hint: HydroGel acts like water for nearby farmland.
goals.why: Hydrates farmland like water, without water holes in your field.
steps: Craft HydroGel (recipe below).
Place it where the water would go: it hydrates farmland around it.

goals.text: Build a Cooking Table kitchen
goals.hint: The cooking table lists every meal you can make from connected counters, fridges and jars.
goals.why: Shows every food you can make from your stored ingredients and crafts it in one click.
steps: Craft the Cooking Table (recipe below).
Place counters, a fridge and cabinets touching it; it reads their contents.

goals.text: Capture a Cow in a Jar
goals.hint: Place a milk jar, lead a cow above it and drop an anvil on the cow for endless milk.
goals.why: Endless milk for your kitchen, cakes and potion cures.
steps: Place a Milk Jar.
Lead a cow onto the jar (hold wheat).
Drop an anvil on the cow: it shrinks into the jar.

obtain.cookingforblockheads:cow_jar: Not crafted: lead a cow onto a Milk Jar and drop an anvil on it.

goals.text: Use Roosts to automate resource collection from Chickens
goals.hint: Catch chickens with the Catcher, breed new kinds, and put them in a Roost to collect their drops.
goals.why: Resource chickens lay iron, gold, redstone, diamonds and more: renewable resources with no work.
steps: Craft a Catcher and a Roost.
Right-click a chicken with the catcher to get it as an item.
Put chickens in the roost; they lay their resource into its output.
JEI shows how to breed each chicken (press R on a chicken item).

goals.text: Breed new Chickens in a Breeder and gather drops with a Collector
goals.hint: The Breeder makes new chicken types; the Collector pulls items out of nearby roosts.
goals.why: Breeding unlocks better resource chickens; the collector gathers everything in one place.
steps: Put two parent chickens and seeds in the breeder.
Place a collector near your roosts and pull items out with a hopper.

goals.text: Craft a Lexica Botania
goals.hint: The Lexica explains all of Botania. Mystical flowers give the petals you need.
goals.why: Botania is flower magic: mana, automation, tools and the Gaia Guardian boss. The Lexica is its full in-game manual.
steps: Find mystical flowers (colorful glowing flowers in forests and plains) and get petals from them.
Craft the Lexica from a book and a sapling (recipe below).

goals.text: Craft a Petal Apothecary
goals.hint: Fill it with water and throw in petals and seeds to make special flowers.
goals.why: Every functional Botania flower (generating and functional) is made in the apothecary.
steps: Craft the apothecary (cobblestone and petals).
Fill it with a water bucket.
Throw in the petals of a recipe, then a seed: the flower pops out.

goals.text: Create Livingwood and Livingrock with a Pure Daisy
goals.hint: Place logs or stone around a Pure Daisy and wait.
goals.why: Livingwood and livingrock build mana spreaders, pools and the runic altar.
steps: Make a Pure Daisy in the apothecary (4 white petals + seed).
Place it and put logs or stone in the 8 blocks around it.
Wait about a minute: they turn into livingwood and livingrock.

diagram.title: Pure Daisy
diagram.view: Top view
diagram.note: Any mix of logs and stone works.

obtain.minecraft:oak_log: Chop any tree; every kind of log works.
obtain.minecraft:stone: Smelt cobblestone in a furnace, or mine stone with a Silk Touch pickaxe.

goals.text: Craft a Mortar and Pestle
goals.hint: Roots grinds herbs in the mortar for spells.
goals.why: The Mortar and Pestle processes ingredients for Roots recipes.
steps: Craft the Mortar and Pestle.
Open a mortar recipe in JEI and place its listed ingredients into the Mortar.
Use the Pestle on the Mortar until processing finishes, then collect the result.

goals.text: Build a Pyre and perform a ritual
goals.hint: Place a ritual's ingredients in a Pyre and ignite it.
goals.why: Rituals summon rain, speed up crops, heal, repel monsters and more, for a few minutes at a time.
steps: Craft and place the Pyre in a clear work area.
Choose a ritual in JEI, check its conditions and place the listed ingredients into the Pyre.
Ignite it with Flint and Steel and verify the ritual effect.
Keep the affected area within its displayed range.

goals.text: Craft a Grove Crafter
goals.hint: Grove crafters make nature items near a grove stone.
goals.why: Makes Roots items like wildwood tools, the staff and spell ingredients.
steps: Craft the grove crafter and place it near a Grove Stone.
Put the recipe ingredients on it (JEI) and activate it.

goals.text: Choose and cast a Roots spell with a Staff
goals.hint: Open the Roots Spell Library to configure a spell on your Staff.
goals.why: Spells heal you, attack mobs, grow plants, light areas and more, from a distance.
goals.tip: The pinned Roots 4 uses the Spell Library and staff spell slots. Do not follow older spell-powder instructions.
steps: Craft the Staff using its JEI recipe.
Hold it and use the Open Spell Library binding shown in its tooltip or Controls.
Choose an available spell, meet its unlock requirements and assign it to a staff slot.
Provide the spell's required herbs or other costs, select that slot and use the Staff to cast.

goals.text: Collect Inferium Essence from Inferium Ore or mobs
goals.hint: Inferium ore generates underground; mobs also drop essence.
goals.why: Mystical Agriculture grows resources (iron, gold, diamonds ...) as crops. Inferium essence is its base currency.
steps: Mine Inferium Ore (stone with green flecks) underground.
Kill mobs: they sometimes drop essence too.

goals.text: Craft an Inferium Seed and start an Inferium Essence farm
goals.hint: Plant inferium seeds on farmland; harvesting gives essence to upgrade into better seeds.
goals.why: Inferium crops make more essence, which upgrades into better essences for resource seeds.
goals.tip: Upgrade essence with an Infusion Crystal, not a prosperity shard. JEI shows the four-essence recipes and crystal durability.
steps: Craft Inferium Seeds using JEI.
Plant them on compatible farmland, harvest the essence and keep the farm supplied.
Use four Inferium Essence with an Infusion Crystal to make Prudentium Essence; repeat the appropriate recipes for later tiers.

goals.text: Block attacks with an Apple Shield
goals.hint: Shields made from apples; golden and enchanted versions are stronger.
goals.why: A fun shield upgrade path: the golden and enchanted golden apple shields block more and last longer.
steps: Craft a red apple shield (recipe below).
Hold it in your off-hand and right-click to block.
Upgrade to golden or enchanted golden apple shields later.

goals.text: Craft a Building Wand
goals.hint: Not Enough Wands: places a row or wall of blocks in one click.
goals.why: Extend walls and floors by many blocks in one click: big builds go fast.
steps: Craft the wand (recipe below).
Right-click the face of a wall: it adds a layer using blocks from your inventory. It costs a little XP.

goals.text: Carry a Void Cup to delete junk
goals.hint: Anything you put in the Void Cup is destroyed.
goals.why: Get rid of cobblestone, dirt and junk instantly instead of dropping it (dropped items lag the server).
steps: Craft a Void Cup.
Right-click to open it and put junk inside: it is destroyed.

goals.text: Make a dark room away from your base for spawning mobs and collecting loot
goals.hint: Mobs spawn in darkness. Funnel them into one kill spot.
goals.why: Mob drops (bones, string, gunpowder, ender pearls) and XP are needed constantly. A farm brings them to you.
steps: Build an enclosed dark room (light level 0) at least 24 blocks from where you stand.
Use water streams to push mobs into one corner.
Drop them down a 22-block fall (or into a kill chamber) so you finish them with one hit.

goals.text: Move and damage mobs with Dark Utilities plates
goals.hint: Vector plates push mobs; damage plates hurt them; filters choose which mobs.
goals.why: Plates move mobs without water and can kill them without you being there.
steps: Craft vector plates and damage plates.
Lay vector plates to steer mobs, then damage plates at the kill spot.

goals.text: Explore a Trial Chamber and open an ominous vault
goals.hint: Trial chambers are copper-and-tuff structures underground. Ominous keys come from ominous trials.
goals.why: Trial chambers hold vaults with enchanted books, diamonds and the Heavy Core used for the Mace.
steps: Find one underground (copper and tuff rooms, often seen in caves).
Defeat the trial spawners to get Trial Keys and open vaults.
Drink an Ominous Bottle (from raid captains) to start ominous trials for Ominous Keys.

goals.text: Craft a Mace and learn its falling attack
goals.hint: The heavy core comes from ominous vaults in trial chambers; combine it with a breeze rod.
goals.why: The mace hits harder the further you fall before striking: huge damage against bosses.
steps: Open ominous vaults for a Heavy Core.
Kill Breezes in the trial chamber for Breeze Rods.
Craft the mace and jump onto enemies.

goals.text: Travel to the Nether
goals.hint: Build a 4x5 obsidian frame and light it with flint and steel. Bring spare blocks and food.
goals.why: The Nether has blaze rods, quartz, glowstone, nether wart, wither skeletons and ancient debris. Many mods need its materials.
goals.tip: Beds explode in the Nether; use your Overworld bed for respawning.
steps: Collect ten obsidian and build the upright portal frame shown below.
Light its interior with Flint and Steel.
Bring blocks, food and fire resistance if available, and mark the portal on arrival.
Secure the return portal before exploring.

diagram.title: Nether portal
diagram.view: Side view (stand it upright)
diagram.note: The corners are optional. Light the empty middle with flint and steel.

obtain.minecraft:obsidian: Pour water onto still lava and mine it with a diamond pickaxe, or pour water into a Stone Barrel full of lava.

goals.text: Find a Nether Fortress and collect Blaze Rods
goals.hint: Fortresses are long dark-brick bridges. Blazes spawn near their spawners.
goals.why: Blaze rods make brewing stands, blaze powder, eyes of ender and many machines. Wither skeletons (for the Wither boss) live in fortresses too.
steps: Explore the Nether along one axis (east/west) to find dark red brick bridges.
Find a blaze spawner (a cage with fire) and fight blazes with a shield or bow.
Snowballs hurt blazes; fire resistance makes this much safer.

mobs.where: Blazes live in Nether Fortresses, around blaze spawners (a cage with a tiny spinning blaze inside). Bring fire resistance; snowballs hurt them. Carry a spawner home with Carry On for a blaze farm.

goals.text: Brew a Potion of Fire Resistance
goals.hint: Brewing stand, nether wart in water bottles, then magma cream.
goals.why: Fire resistance makes you immune to fire and lava: essential for the Nether, blaze farms and the Twilight Fire Swamp and Hydra.
steps: Craft a brewing stand (blaze rod + cobblestone) and fuel it with blaze powder.
Get nether wart from a fortress and brew it into water bottles (Awkward Potion).
Add magma cream (slime + blaze powder) for Fire Resistance. Redstone makes it last longer.

mobs.where: Blazes live in Nether Fortresses, around blaze spawners (a cage with a tiny spinning blaze inside). Bring fire resistance; snowballs hurt them. Carry a spawner home with Carry On for a blaze farm.

goals.text: Find a Bastion and trade with Piglins
goals.hint: Wear one gold armor piece and throw gold ingots to piglins to barter.
goals.why: Piglins trade ender pearls, obsidian, fire resistance potions, quartz and more for gold. Bastions hold netherite and gold loot.
steps: Wear at least one piece of gold armor so piglins stay calm.
Throw a gold ingot to a piglin (Q) and pick up what it gives back.

mobs.where: Piglins live in Crimson Forests and the Nether Wastes and guard Bastions. Wear at least one piece of gold armor so they stay calm, then throw them gold ingots to barter.

goals.text: Ride a Strider across a lava ocean
goals.hint: Saddle a Strider and steer it with warped fungus on a stick.
goals.why: A challenge: striders (saddle + warped fungus on a stick) carry you across lava safely.
goals.tip: Ordinary boats do not cross lava safely. Keep a marked return route.
steps: Bring a saddle, warped fungus on a stick, spare blocks and fire resistance.
Find a Strider beside a Nether lava sea, saddle it and mount it.
Hold warped fungus on a stick to steer across the lava, then dismount onto safe ground.

goals.text: Use Carry On to bring a Blaze Spawner home
goals.hint: Sneak-right-click the spawner with empty hands to carry it; it keeps its mob.
goals.why: A blaze spawner at home is an endless blaze rod farm: rods are needed for brewing, eyes of ender and Create brass.
steps: Clear the blazes around the spawner and empty your hands.
Sneak-right-click the spawner to pick it up.
Carry it home and place it in a dark, enclosed room with a kill spot.

goals.text: Grow Natura Nether trees and berries
goals.hint: Use soul-sand sieving recipes to obtain Nether saplings and berries.
goals.why: The pack disables natural Natura tree generation; its recipe and sieve routes keep these materials obtainable.
steps: Collect soul sand in the Nether.
Use JEI to select the soul-sand sieving recipe and mesh for the sapling or berry you want.
Plant the result on its required soil with enough clear space, then harvest and replant.

goals.text: Craft and power a generator of some kind
goals.hint: Simple Generators burn fuel, food or lava for power. They charge machines next to them.
goals.why: Most tech machines run on Forge Energy (FE/RF). A generator is the start of every tech path.
steps: Craft a Furnace Generator (recipe below) or any other generator.
Put coal or charcoal in it.
Place a machine next to it, or connect it with conduits or cables.

goals.text: Build an Extra Utilities generator
goals.hint: Fuel a Survival or Furnace Generator to produce FE for machines.
goals.why: Extra Utilities generators produce machine energy. Grid Power (GP), used by mills and some utility blocks, is a separate system.
steps: Craft a Survival or Furnace Generator.
Insert a fuel accepted by its recipes and connect an FE cable or adjacent compatible machine.
Confirm energy reaches the machine; GP mills do not replace this FE supply.

goals.text: Build Solar Panels from Solar Flux
goals.hint: Panels make power in daylight; neighboring panels share it.
goals.why: Free power during the day with no fuel. Higher tiers produce much more, and neighbouring panels share power.
steps: Craft solar panels (recipe below).
Place them under open sky, touching each other.
Connect one panel to a battery or machines with conduits or cables. A battery keeps power for the night.

goals.text: Store power in an RFTools Power Cell
goals.hint: Power cells store energy; every side starts switched off until you set it with a wrench.
goals.why: A battery stores generator overflow and keeps machines running at night or while generators refuel.
goals.tip: If a new cell stays empty, check its sides with a wrench first.
steps: Craft a power cell (recipe below) and place it between your generators and machines.
Every side starts disabled. Hit a side with a wrench (the RFTools Smart Wrench or another wrench) to cycle it: input, output, off.
Set the sides touching generators or cables to input and the sides feeding machines to output.
Stack cells on top of each other to share capacity.

goals.text: Make a basic Ender IO capacitor and a Machine Chassis
goals.hint: Make the capacitor and chassis with the current JEI recipes; dust sieving supplies Grains of Infinity.
goals.why: Capacitors and chassis are core ingredients for the Ender IO machine path.
steps: Use JEI to gather the capacitor and chassis ingredients.
For Grains of Infinity, check the pack dust-sieving recipe and its required mesh.
Craft the capacitor and chassis, then the Ender IO machine you want.
Install a suitable capacitor where required and supply FE.

goals.text: Make alloys in an Alloy Smelter
goals.hint: Electrical steel and other Ender IO alloys come from the alloy smelter.
goals.why: Ender IO machines, capacitors and conduits all need its alloys (electrical steel, energetic alloy, conductive iron ...).
steps: Craft the alloy smelter (recipe below).
Power it and put ingredients in its three input slots (JEI shows every alloy).

goals.text: Automate turning Cobblestone into Gravel with a SAG Mill or Auto Hammer
goals.hint: The SAG Mill also doubles ore. The Auto Hammer works like a powered hammer.
goals.why: Crushing ore into two dusts doubles your metal, and gravel feeds the sieves.
steps: Craft a SAG Mill (or an Auto Hammer).
Power it and feed cobblestone or ores in; take the output with a hopper or conduit.

goals.text: Use Ender IO Conduits to power several machines at once
goals.hint: Conduits carry power, items and fluids in a single block.
goals.why: One conduit line can carry power, items, fluids and redstone together, keeping your workshop tidy.
steps: Craft energy conduits.
Run a line from a generator past your machines; it connects to each one.
Later add item and fluid conduits into the same blocks.

goals.text: Process an ore piece into ingots with an Actually Additions Crusher
goals.hint: Use an Actually Additions Crusher, then smelt its dust output.
goals.why: Ore doubling: each raw ore becomes two dusts, which smelt into two ingots.
goals.tip: Yields vary by recipe; do not assume every input always doubles.
steps: Craft the Crusher and connect FE.
Look up your exact ore or raw-material recipe in JEI and check its yield.
Feed the accepted input, collect the dust, and smelt it into ingots.

goals.text: Convert blocks with an Atomic Reconstructor
goals.hint: Its laser converts the block in front of it; lenses change the effect.
goals.why: Makes Actually Additions crystals (needed for its machines) and converts many items with lenses.
steps: Craft and power the reconstructor.
Place a block in front of it or throw items into its beam path.
JEI lists every conversion.

goals.text: Make Steel with a Coke Oven and Blast Furnace
goals.hint: The coke oven makes coal coke; the blast furnace turns iron and coke into steel.
goals.why: Steel is used by Immersive Engineering and many other machines; coal coke is a strong fuel.
steps: Craft the Engineer's Hammer and read the Engineer's Manual.
Build a 3x3x3 cube of 27 Coke Bricks and hit the middle of a side with the hammer.
Burn coal into coal coke. Then build a 3x3x3 Blast Furnace (27 blast bricks) and smelt iron with coke into steel.

diagram.title: Coke Oven
diagram.view: A solid 3x3x3 cube of Coke Bricks; hit the middle of one side with the hammer.
diagram.note: The Blast Furnace is the same cube made of Blast Bricks.

goals.text: Build and power an Immersive Engineering Crusher
goals.hint: Follow the Engineer's Manual structure, form it with the hammer, and supply FE.
goals.why: The Crusher processes supported ores and other materials. Metal-equipment recycling belongs to the Arc Furnace.
steps: Open the Crusher entry in the Engineer's Manual and assemble its shown multiblock.
Use the Engineer's Hammer on the indicated trigger block to form it.
Connect FE to its energy input and provide output storage.
Feed an accepted item into the top and collect the result; keep yourself out of the machinery.

obtain.immersiveengineering:crusher: Not crafted: build the multiblock shown in the Engineer's Manual and hit it with the Engineer's Hammer.

goals.text: Make Brass using a Blaze-heated Mechanical Mixer
goals.hint: Catch a blaze in an empty blaze burner and place it under the basin.
goals.why: Brass unlocks Create's advanced parts: brass funnels, mechanical arms, precision mechanisms and trains.
steps: Craft an empty blaze burner and right-click a blaze with it (or capture one at a spawner).
Place it under your basin and feed it fuel.
Put copper and zinc ingots in the basin under a running mixer.

goals.text: Craft a Mana Pool and a Mana Spreader
goals.hint: Generating flowers make mana; spreaders send it to pools.
goals.why: Mana powers all of Botania: infusing manasteel and mana diamonds, crafting runes, Terrasteel and the Gaia ritual.
steps: Make a generating flower (Endoflame burns fuel, Hydroangeas uses water).
Place a mana spreader near the flower; bind the flower to it with the Wand of the Forest.
Aim the spreader at a mana pool (bind spreader to pool with the wand).

diagram.title: First mana setup
diagram.view: Top view
diagram.note: Flowers within 6 blocks of the spreader. Feed Endoflames coal or logs by dropping them next to them.

goals.text: Craft a Wand of the Forest
goals.hint: The wand binds flowers and spreaders and shows mana.
goals.why: Needed to link flowers, spreaders and pools and to activate many Botania blocks.
steps: Craft the Wand of the Forest.
Switch it to Bind Mode using its tooltip controls.
Sneak-right-click the Mana Spreader, then sneak-right-click the intended Mana Pool to bind them.
Use the wand on the spreader and pool to inspect their connection and mana.

goals.text: Infuse Manasteel in a Mana Pool
goals.hint: Drop an iron ingot into a Mana Pool with enough mana for the recipe.
goals.why: Manasteel makes Botania tools and armor; manasteel, mana diamonds and mana pearls are the three Terrasteel ingredients.
goals.tip: The pool does not need to be completely full. Each conversion consumes only its recipe cost.
steps: Generate mana with flowers and send it to a Mana Pool through a bound spreader.
Check the Manasteel recipe and make sure the pool has enough mana.
Drop an iron ingot into the pool and collect the converted ingot.

goals.text: Craft and Place a Blood Altar
goals.hint: Use a Sacrificial Dagger next to the altar to fill it with your blood (LP).
goals.why: Blood Magic turns your health (Life Points) into powerful sigils, rituals and armor.
steps: Craft a sacrificial dagger and the blood altar.
Right-click the dagger while standing next to the altar to put blood in (it costs health; eat well).
Put items in the altar to transmute them with LP.

goals.text: Fill a Weak Blood Orb
goals.hint: Put a diamond in the filled altar to make a Weak Blood Orb, then right-click it to bind it.
goals.why: The orb stores your LP network. Sigils and rituals draw on it, and every altar tier needs a better orb.
steps: Fill the altar with at least 2000 LP.
Put a diamond in the altar: it becomes a Weak Blood Orb.
Right-click the orb to bind it to you, then leave it in the altar to fill.

goals.text: Make Blank Slates in the Blood Altar
goals.hint: Stone placed in a filled altar becomes a blank slate.
goals.why: Blank slates craft blood runes, and runes raise the altar to higher tiers for better orbs, sigils and armor.
steps: Put stone into the filled altar.
Keep it filled until the stone becomes a blank slate.
Craft blood runes from slates and stone.

diagram.title: Tier 2 altar
diagram.view: Eight runes one block below the altar, all around it.
diagram.note: The 8 runes go one level lower than the altar, all around it. Higher tiers need more runes and pillars (see the Blood Magic guide).

goals.text: Craft a Sigil and bind it to your Blood Orb
goals.hint: Craft a sigil in the Alchemy Table using the required bound Blood Orb and LP.
goals.why: Sigils are reusable magic tools powered by your LP: the Divination Sigil shows your LP, others give water, lava, air jumps, an item magnet and more.
goals.tip: This port uses Alchemy Table sigil recipes. Do not look for an older-version altar or alchemy-array recipe.
steps: Right-click your Blood Orb to bind it to you, then charge your soul network through the Blood Altar.
Open the sigil recipe in JEI and note the required orb tier and LP cost.
Put the ingredients and bound orb into the Alchemy Table and let the craft finish.
Bind or activate the resulting sigil as its tooltip directs.

goals.text: Collect Demonic Will in a Petty Tartaric Gem
goals.hint: Carry a Petty Tartaric Gem while killing hostile monsters to collect Will.
goals.why: Demonic Will powers the Hellfire Forge and Will-based tools, armor and rituals.
goals.tip: This port collects Will from monster kills while carrying a gem; a Sentient Sword or snare is not required.
steps: Build a Hellfire Forge and use the Petty Tartaric Gem recipe: glass, gold, redstone and lapis.
This first gem recipe needs no stored Will.
